name: SOMALIA

flag.title: The Star & Sky
flag.note: Blue field with a white five-pointed star

lead: Somalia juts like a number 7 from Africa's horn into the Indian Ocean — mainland Africa's longest coastline at 3,300 km. Camels outnumber cars, ancient cave paintings glow near Hargeisa, and Somali poets have recited epics by campfire for a thousand years. A land rebuilding itself, full of colour, music, and desert pride.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Largest city, on the Indian Ocean

sections.geography: A horn, a sea & desert skies

geo: Somalia is the very tip of the Horn of Africa — the pointy bit poking furthest east into the Indian Ocean. Its northern mountains hold Shimbiris at 2,416 m, while most of the country is flat, hot thorn-scrub savanna baked by the sun.

Two rivers — the Jubba and the Shabelle — flow down from Ethiopia and give farmers the only green strips in an otherwise arid landscape. Dry monsoon winds carve sandy plains and rocky gorges across this wide, sun-scorched land.
animals: Somalia has more camels than any other country — over 7 million dromedaries wander its plains, giving families milk, transport, and wealth. The gerenuk, a long-necked antelope, stands on its hind legs to nibble high branches.
The critically endangered Somali wild ass, ancestor of the donkey, still roams the rocky north. Offshore, whale sharks and sea turtles glide past barely-explored Indian Ocean reefs.
culture: Somalis are so celebrated for poetry that scholars call theirs a 'Nation of Poets'. Verses are memorised and recited at weddings, markets, and peace talks — words carry real power here. Music uses a pentatonic scale and the warm tones of the oud lute.

Hospitality is sacred: every guest gets shaah (sweet spiced tea) and canjeero, a spongy sourdough flatbread eaten with honey or stew. Women wear the colourful guntiino wrap; men the macawis sarong — bright stripes for every occasion.
history: Somali trading cities like Zeila and Mogadishu were busy Arab sea-trade ports over a thousand years ago, swapping gold, ivory, and frankincense. Cave paintings at Laas Geel near Hargeisa show decorated cattle painted 5,000–9,000 years ago.

Somalia was split between British and Italian colonial rulers in the 1800s, then united as an independent country on 1 July 1960. Civil war from 1991 shattered the state, but a federal government was restored and the country has been slowly rebuilding since the 2010s.
wows: Somalia's mainland coastline tops 3,300 km — the longest of any country on mainland Africa.
Laas Geel cave paintings are up to 9,000 years old — among the best-preserved rock art on Earth.
Somalia holds over 7 million camels — more than any other country on the planet.
Somali only got an official written script in 1972, yet has one of Africa's richest oral poetry traditions.
The flag's five-pointed star stands for five regions where Somali people live across four countries.
Somali songs use only five notes per octave, giving the music a haunting, ancient sound.
Mogadishu was a thriving trading city 1,000+ years ago, visited by the explorer Ibn Battuta in 1331.

myths.fact: Piracy peaked around 2011 and has since fallen sharply — the High Risk Area was lifted in 2023, and most of Somalia's long coast is peacefully fished by local communities.
The north has green mountain ranges and the south has two rivers with fertile farmland; even the dry plains turn vivid green after the spring rains.
